claims: Probe branch name can collide (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:192`): `$(date +%s)-$$` isn't unique; containers have their own process-ID numbering, so two fresh containers can easily get the same ID
On a probe branch collision, one setup deletes the branch and the other's delete at `:217` fails, so that setup aborts claiming it couldn't delete its own probe
If `HEAD` differs on a probe branch collision, the second push is rejected and prints the wrong message ("cannot create… give Contents read/write")

Runbook doesn't list OS package repos (`docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:61-70`): `--with-deps` runs `apt-get update/install` against the image's package repos, and those hosts aren't in the list that claims to be what setup needs (same gap for the `gh` apt install path)

Playwright install now blocks all of setup (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:537`, called at `:583`): unlike `claude-code-web-setup.sh:141-153` and `scripts/setup.sh:144`, it fails the whole setup in Codex Cloud, so any environment without Playwright CDN and apt access can't start any task after merge

The pull-request check doesn't prove what the runbook requires (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:184-185`): the probe only does a GET on the open-PR list, so a token with Contents write but PR read-only passes setup, then fails at `gh pr create` during ship
If the repo is public, even the PR read check can't fail, since any token can list PRs

The probe branch may create a Vercel preview deployment: `ui-dashboard/vercel.json` only turns off deployments for `sentry-autofix/*`, so every setup pushes a branch Vercel will look at, producing an 'ignored' deployment record or a real preview build that may fail because the branch is deleted within seconds
The "created but couldn't delete" branch (`:217-221`) isn't tested
The existing write-probe tests use a fake `git`, so they prove nothing about real push behavior

judge_reasoning.3846756487: The review's missed-item 2 says the PR probe only GETs the PR list, while the runbook requires read/write, so a token with PR read-only access passes.
judge_reasoning.3846756810: The review never raises the missing non-github.com origin guard in verify_github_api_capabilities or verify_origin_write_access.
judge_reasoning.3846756918: The review says the opposite: it clears cleanup logic ('created is reset on both delete paths') and does not flag the lost EXIT-trap fallback after a failed delete.
judge_reasoning.3846756922: The review confirms the probe branch name `$(date +%s)-$$` isn't unique because of container PID reuse, describes the resulting collisions, and suggests a random suffix.
judge_reasoning.3846757143: The review never suggests `git push --dry-run` or objects to mutating origin. Its Vercel point is a different side effect.
judge_reasoning.3846757191: The review confirms the runbook's outbound list omits the OS apt package repos needed by `playwright install --with-deps`.

1.why: Line 192 `probe_branch="codex-cloud-write-probe-$(date +%s)-$$"`; the known defect at codex-cloud-setup.sh:192 already says to make the branch name globally unique.

2.why: Deleting a branch that is already gone makes the `git push origin --delete` at :217 fail and return 1. This is a consequence of the name collision already covered by the known :192 uniqueness defect.

3.why: The rejected create push at :206 does print the Contents read/write message, but it only happens after a name collision. That root cause is the known :192 uniqueness defect.

4.why: The docs outbound-access list (md:61-70) has no OS/apt package repos. This matches the known docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:70 'Document the distribution package source'.

5.why: `install_playwright_host_dependencies` is called plainly under `set -euo pipefail`, so any failure stops setup. claude-code-web-setup.sh:147-152 and scripts/setup.sh:145-150 wrap the same command in `if ! ...; then warn` and keep going. Blocked CDN or apt access aborts Codex setup unless someone opts out.

6.why: Lines 184-185 only GET `pulls?state=open&per_page=1`, even though the docs ask for PR read/write. This is the known :195 'Verify pull-request write access' defect.

7.why: This extends the same PR-read-only probe weakness (GET on /pulls) that the known :195 defect already covers.

8.why: vercel.json only disables `sentry-autofix/*`, but the concern is side effects of the probe mutating origin on every run, which the known :231 P3 covers. Also, ignore-build.sh would normally skip because HEAD matches main and changes no dashboard paths.

9.why: The test file has no case that calls or stubs `verify_github_api_capabilities` (grep finds no matches). The new API probe steps have no test coverage.

10.why: The only tests are origin-write-access (git always succeeds) and origin-write-access-refused (git always fails, so the create step fails first). No case covers create succeeding and delete failing, which is exactly where the known cleanup-fallback bug sits.

11.why: Stubbing `git` in unit tests is the file's normal pattern (it also stubs pnpm). The claim names no specific behavior the fakes miss, beyond a general preference for integration tests.
